lesson_title: Building Plans and Models: from Paper House to Packed Carton
hook_text: The box's volume says 61 cans fit. Try to pack them and you stop at 48. Where did 13 cans go?
clip_script: Floor plan, scale 1 to 100. Roof off, viewed from above. That bedroom is 35 millimetres on paper — add two zeros — 3 500 millimetres. 3,5 metres of real brick. The 9-millimetre gap? A 900 door, standard. Now shop the room. Floor: 10,5 square metres, plus ten percent for cuts, in 2,2-a-box flooring — 5,25 boxes, so buy 6. Skirting: 13 metres around, minus the doorway, 12,1 — sold in threes, buy 5 lengths. Paint: walls are 13 times 2,6, minus door and window, times TWO coats — 60,4 squares — two big tins. R3 649, priced off a piece of paper. Now the spaza delivery. Carton: 42 by 28 by 22. Cans: 7 wide, 11 tall. Divide the volumes and you get 61 cans. Wrong. Cans don't melt. Count instead: 6 along, 4 across — 24 a layer — 2 layers. Forty-eight. The missing 13 cans? They were never cans — just the air trapped between circles and corners, a fifth of the box. Count reality, not volume.
visual_style: A floor plan unfolding into a 3D room as measurements inflate a hundredfold; shelves stacking flooring boxes and paint tins with prices; then a transparent carton filling with cans, the ghostly 13 phantom cans dissolving into blue air gaps.
mood: Builder's confidence — paper in one hand, tape measure in the other.
pacing: Steady through the scale conversion, brisk through the shopping list, a hard stop on the wrong 61, and a satisfying count to 48.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and price a room — or pack a van — straight off the plan.
